issues.description: The problem statement (UML and description) requires a method named calculateTotalPrice(Meal) (and states it must be static), but both the template comments and the solution implement and call a method named computeMealCost(Meal) instead. This name/signature mismatch between the specification and the code will confuse students about which method to implement and may cause tests or examples to reference a different method name than students provide.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name across problem statement, template, and solution. Either rename computeMealCost(Meal) in the solution and template to calculateTotalPrice(Meal) (keeping it static and returning int), or update the problem statement and UML to require computeMealCost(Meal). Update example usages in Main accordingly so all artifacts reference the same method name.

issues.description: The problem statement requires a static method named calculateTotalPrice(Meal) to compute a meal's total cost, but the provided code (both the solution SealSaloon and the template Main comment) uses the name computeMealCost(...) for the same functionality. This mismatch can confuse students about which method name to implement or call and how to map the requirement to the code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier consistent across artifacts. Either rename the method in code (SealSaloon.computeMealCost -> SealSaloon.calculateTotalPrice and update Main) or update the problem statement to refer to computeMealCost. Ensure method signature and static-ness match the problem description.
